This case presents a classic triad of acute-onset symmetric annular/targetoid rash, low-grade fever, and arthralgias — all emerging 7 days after amoxicillin initiation. The presence of a single targetoid lesion with central clearing (a hallmark of erythema multiforme) *plus* periorbital edema is highly instructive. DRESS syndrome often manifests 2–6 weeks post-drug (though earlier onset—up to 10% as early as day 7—is documented), and periorbital edema is a recognized early sign reflecting systemic inflammation and capillary leak. CBC may not yet show eosinophilia (can lag by several days), making clinical diagnosis essential at this stage. Thus, while EM is plausible, DRESS better accounts for the *systemic* features (fever, arthralgias, periorbital edema) and timing — and carries higher morbidity if missed.

Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS)
